output.title: Measuring late payment terms without guessing
output.body:
If you want to measure late payment terms, keep the decision narrow: are you still tracking due dates, actual payment dates, and follow-up status by memory or spreadsheet, or do you have a repeatable check that flags overdue invoices before they turn into a cash-flow surprise?

The useful first step is not to redesign finance. It is to define one bounded workflow: compare the invoice date, agreed terms, and payment date; flag anything past due; and keep a simple log of what was late. Any collection action stays human-approved. Money movement stays human. That boundary matters.

If your current process depends on manual review, the real question is whether the workflow is frequent and repeatable enough to justify automation. Ask yourself: how many invoices do you issue each month, and how do you currently know which ones are late?

Then audit one week of invoices. Note which were paid on time, which were late, and how long the manual review took. That gives you a concrete picture of the work before you decide whether a bounded pilot is worth setting up. No drama, just less guessing.
